prompt:
Premium commercial monochrome game UI for an original modern Korean urban life simulation called Ian Growing.

The interface uses an almost entirely achromatic palette: black, near-black, charcoal, gray, light gray, off-white and white.

No colorful mobile-game interface.

Modern high-end pixel-art UI with crisp geometric borders, restrained industrial design, intentional negative space, precise alignment, strong typography hierarchy, clean iconography and extremely clear interactive states.

The interface should feel cold, urban, slightly bureaucratic and subtly humorous, supporting the game's understated black comedy about work, debt, education, money and adulthood.

Use contrast, typography, inversion, line weight, patterns, iconography and animation instead of bright colors to communicate hierarchy and state.

Selected elements may invert from black to white.

Important numbers should be large and highly readable.

Secondary information should use muted gray.

The UI must support Korean text with excellent readability.

Cohesive with a detailed 2.5D pixel-art open world.

Professional commercial PC/console game quality.

Not a website.
Not a SaaS dashboard.
Not glossy mobile-game UI.
Not fantasy.
Not cyberpunk.
No colorful gradients.
No rainbow rarity system.
No gold ornamental fantasy frames.
No excessive rounded cards.
No imitation of an existing game's exact interface.

Remove all chromatic accent colors.
Use only black, white, off-white and neutral gray values.
Preserve the exact layout and hierarchy.
Replace color-based state indicators with contrast, border weight, icons and inversion.
The palette chip strip and all samples are strictly neutral. The art-direction board itself should be fully achromatic even in the small world reference previews; original game world remains colored in Unity.
